curation.assessment_origin: External ChatGPT Pro literature report supplied by Carson; transferred with explicit missing-bridge review by the computational agent

component_meanings.E: disease-applicable efficacy evidence, capped for indirect bridges
component_meanings.S: author judgment of pediatric/cancer suitability, not a safety gate
component_meanings.F: feasibility judgment for a decisive first experiment

curation.warning: Scores are externally judged laboratory priorities, not algorithmic predictions or efficacy probabilities; all exact-genotype rescue and clinical gates are unknown.
curation.scenario: Working trans hypothesis; cis remains unresolved and changes the allele-rescue premise
curation.selection_warning: One-point component changes can alter ordering. Arimoclomol and azithromycin are co-leads for an experiment, not proven superior treatments
curation.convergence_note: No positive independent computational rescue line; stability and LINCS screens supply no rescue bonus

proposed_path.edge: arimoclomol → augmented stress/chaperone response in an opsin model
augmented chaperone response → useful N1002K BubR1 → fewer segregation errors

missing_bridges: N1002K abundance, per-molecule activity and phase remain unmeasured
A protein-quantity strategy requires enough residual useful protein; computational stability methods do not establish major destabilization
Feasible free exposure and RMS safety in the exact genotype remain unverified

contrary_evidence.claim: Arimoclomol did not correct cholesterol storage in one NPC1 fibroblast context; responses are context dependent
HSF1 can support malignant survival; this is a counter-screen rationale, not proof that arimoclomol causes RMS

evidence.next_experiment: Compare matched-expression WT and N1002K cells; measure protein half-life, MCC/attachment function and errors per completed division, with an RMS counter-screen at justified exposure.

proposed_path.edge: macrolide exposure → PTC bypass/protein restoration in analogous experimental systems
azithromycin → Leu737Ter readthrough → functional full-length BubR1 → fewer segregation errors

missing_bridges: No demonstrated BUB1B or exact-genotype readthrough rescue
NMD may remove allele-A RNA; readthrough may insert an unsuitable amino acid at 737
Analogous protein signals do not establish allele-specific readthrough at clinically attainable free exposure
Chronic antibacterial stewardship, QT/hepatic/hearing risk and RMS compatibility remain unresolved

contrary_evidence.claim: Non-aminoglycoside PTC responses are weaker/context dependent in another reporter study

evidence.next_experiment: Use endogenous NMD-competent Leu737Ter cells; quantify allele-A RNA and allele-resolved full-length product, then segregation errors with normal-stop, proliferation and mitochondrial controls.

proposed_path.edge: niacin → increased NAD in adults with mitochondrial myopathy
SIRT2/NAD regulation → BubR1 abundance; NMN and SIRT2 transgene were the separate tested interventions
prescription niacin → balanced K668/K250 regulation → useful N1002K BubR1 → fewer segregation errors

missing_bridges: No demonstrated prescription-niacin-to-functional-BubR1 or MVA rescue
Niacin, nicotinamide, NR and NMN are different interventions; transgene survival evidence is not niacin efficacy
Net SIRT2 effects at K668 and K250, baseline NAD sufficiency and N1002K rescue remain unknown
Pediatric ER formulation, free exposure, hepatic/metabolic safety and RMS direction remain unresolved

contrary_evidence.claim: SIRT2 also deacetylates BubR1 K250; simple stability direction is incomplete
SIRT1/SIRT2 expression supports RMS cell survival in a cell study; NAD enhancement is not established cancer protective

evidence.next_experiment: Measure NAD, SIRT2 dependence, K668/K250 acetylation, allele-resolved useful protein and errors per division; require a matched RMS safety counter-screen.
